newsitem.title: USA: Lawyer's emotional appeal rivets Simpson trial.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer's emotional appeal rivets Simpson trial.

text.p: A lawyer for the plaintiffs ended his closing argument in the O.J. Simpson civil trial on Wednesday with an emotional appeal to the jury to compensate a father for the loss of his slain son.
"There is no greater loss than that of a child and it is no less when that child grows into a young man," Daniel Petrocelli said of murder victim Ronald Goldman.

Asking the jury to find ex-football star Simpson responsible for the murder of Goldman, he said Fred Goldman should be compensated for the loss of his son. However, he did not specify a dollar figure.
As the older Goldman sobbed quietly in the courtroom, Petrocelli said the father would never see "the gleaming look of satisfaction on Ron's face as he ushered him into his new restaurant.
"Never sit down at a July the Fourth barbecue, or a Passover, or a birthday. Never have the joy of going to the hospital to see his grandchild."
Ending two days of his closing arguments, Petrocelli pointed to Simpson and said: "There is nothing he can do to bring him back."

Simpson was acquitted in criminal court in October 1995 of murdering his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman. He could be forced to pay the victims' families millions of dollars in damages if found responsible for the killings in the civil trial.

After showing the jury one more time a video of Ronald Goldman and his father at a birthday party less than a year before his June 12, 1994, murder, Petrocelli quoted a 16th century poet about the relationship between a father and son.
"My lovely, living boy, my hope, my happiness, my love, my life," he said. Then turning to the jury he said: "Fred Goldman's lovely living boy is no more."
Attorney John Kelly, who represents the estate of Nicole Brown Simpson, later began his closing arguments in the case.
